title: Learning Rate Transfer in Normalized Transformers
claim: The baseline's optimal learning rate drifts with model size, while our reparameterization keeps the optimum stable and performance equal or better.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend format, red stars mark optima
description: Two side-by-side line plots show validation loss (y-axis) against base learning rate on a log2 x-axis. Each plot has seven colored curves, one per model size, from 8 to 22. A legend under each plot lists the size with its best loss and standard error in parentheses. Panel (a), labeled nGPT (baseline), shows U-shaped curves whose minima, marked with red stars, move to the right as models get larger. The largest models also show widening shaded variance bands and a sharp spike at high learning rates. Panel (b), labeled νGPT (ours), shows smooth, evenly spaced U-curves whose red-star minima line up at nearly the same learning rate. The eye goes first to the scattered stars on the left and the aligned stars on the right.
caption: Different model sizes at fixed aspect ratio nlayers = nheads (in the legend, with the best loss in parentheses) and “compute-optimal” 20 tokens per parameter. The baseline nGPT does not show learning rate transfer. Our parametrization νGPT does, and performs no worse or slightly better. The points are averaged over three initialization seeds and no validation loss EMA is used.
abstract: The Normalized Transformer, or nGPT (arXiv:2410.01131) achieves impressive training speedups and does not require weight decay or learning rate warmup. However, despite having hyperparameters that explicitly scale with model size, we observe that nGPT does not exhibit learning rate transfer across model dimension and token horizon. To rectify this, we combine numerical experiments with a principled use of alignment exponents (arXiv:2407.05872) to revisit and modify the $Î¼$P approach to hyperparameter transfer (arXiv:2011.14522). The result is a novel nGPT parameterization we call $Î½$GPT. Through extensive empirical validation, we find $Î½$GPT exhibits learning rate transfer across width, depth, and token horizon.
